body:
Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The big local story today is Bakersfield College's celebration of the 50th anniversary of its 1976 Junior Rose Bowl championship, capped by a 40-21 Renegade win at Memorial Stadium. Outside, expect a mild November day — a high near 75, a low around 51 tonight, no active weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 82. Deputies had a busy night on the county side, and we'll walk through it below.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came from the county side of 7th Standard Road, where deputies were sent at 10:43 p.m. to the area of 7th Standard Road and Mayer Avenue for shots fired. A caller told dispatchers two people were shooting and trying to shoot his brother. Deputies reported no injuries so far, said the suspects might still be in the area, and noted that a victim was hiding in a field nearby. They asked for a drone and, at 11:01 p.m., began searching for shell casings.

Deputies were back out about three hours later at the Edison Trailer Park on Edison Highway, where a 17-year-old was reported to have been hit with glass and had facial injuries. The man suspected of the assault left on foot. Earlier in the evening, just before 7:30 p.m., a vehicle hit a juvenile on Edison Highway westbound at Fairfax Road north, leaving one patient down in the roadway, and fire crews and medics responded. A separate domestic disturbance at 10:28 p.m. ended with the man who threatened the caller walking out before officers arrived.

Two burglaries in progress stood out in the log: a man in a black hooded sweatshirt seen on camera at the Dollar Tree on the 2,500 block of South 8th Street at 8:32 p.m., and a man on a bicycle seen on camera at a Toyota dealership at 4:59 a.m. Fire crews ran a working fire behind a home on the 5500 block of Woodmere Drive in southwest Bakersfield at 12:48 a.m., smoke reported inside a one-story apartment complex on the 1,600 block of East 11th Street in east Bakersfield at 3:58 a.m., and vehicle fires on Panama Road and Muller Road in southeast Bakersfield.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 75 degrees today and a low around 51 tonight. It's currently 66 degrees at Meadows Field, according to the National Weather Service. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported. Air quality is 82, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's worth keeping an eye on it as the day warms up. All in all, a good Sunday to be outside.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Bakersfield College closed out its regular season with a 40-21 win over College of the Canyons at Memorial Stadium — and did it on a night set aside for history.** Fifty years ago, the Renegades won the 1976 Junior Rose Bowl, and some of those players returned to the stadium Saturday to mark the anniversary. Among them was Michael Georgino, who told the station that walking back in felt like yesterday, even though 50 years is a long time. He remembered playing in front of crowds of more than 18,000. Athletic Director Lynn Kennedy said this year also marks the program's 100th football season, which made the reunion even more meaningful. The current team ends the regular season on a four-game winning streak at 6-4 and is expected to play in a bowl game for the first time since 2024.

**According to 23ABC, a Bakersfield senior living community honored World War II veterans Saturday, including a 105-year-old former British tail gunner.** Bayshire Riverwalk Senior Living held a Veterans Day tribute, and among those recognized was Ron Holdsworth, who turned 105 this year and flew as a tail gunner in a British bomber during the war. His great-great niece, Angie Burns, attended and spoke about his service, noting he completed 32 operational missions, including flights over France and Holland and deep into Germany, with his final combat flight in January 1944 over West Berlin. Holdsworth received a replica of the Royal Air Force uniform he wore in 1944 and put it on during the ceremony.

**23ABC also spent time at the Park at River Walk, where the ALS Network held its annual family day and walk on Nov. 7.** ALS, or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, is a neurodegenerative disease that affects motor skills and eventually leads to loss of muscle function, and it affects roughly 35,000 people in the United States each year. The network provides resources, advocacy, and care services for people with ALS and their families. Jeff Hurlbert, a Kern County resident living with ALS, told the station that the disease "takes and takes and takes," but that it also gives — "the tenderness of the heart." Attendees enjoyed free food, coffee and hot chocolate, and a kids' activity center with snow cones. Network leaders said awareness is the most important part of their work.

**Bakersfield Now reports that two suspects have been arrested in connection with a deadly Halloween party shooting, according to the Kern County Sheriff's Office.** Few details were available beyond the arrests, and we'll share more as the case develops.

**KGET 17 reports that two people were struck by a hit-and-run driver on Edison Highway, and one of them has died, according to the California Highway Patrol.** The crash remains under investigation.

**KGET 17 also notes that shorter daylight hours can trigger depression, and shares some practical ways to fight it.** With clocks turned back and sunset arriving earlier, it's a timely reminder for anyone who feels the seasonal shift more than most.

## Something good

Fifty years after hoisting the Junior Rose Bowl trophy, the men who wore those Renegade uniforms got to walk back into Memorial Stadium on Saturday night and watch the current team win 40-21. The college marked both the 50th anniversary of that 1976 title and its 100th football season in one evening — a rare chance to see a program's whole history standing on the same field. The Renegades close the regular season 6-4 and bowl-bound for the first time since 2024.

## Coming up this week

Monday is a busy one at City Hall. The Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m., and the Youth Commission meets at 4:30 p.m. Both are open to the public, and agendas are posted ahead of time if you want to look before you go.

Over at the Fox Theater, the calendar is full. Today brings the 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer EXPO, and Monday night the Cults & Classics series screens "Play Misty for Me." Later in the week, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet takes the stage on Nov. 13, followed by the 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards on Nov. 15. The Cults & Classics series continues Nov. 23 with "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?", and season passes for the 2026-2027 run are already on sale.

And a note for the week ahead: Veterans Day falls midweek, so watch for ceremony schedules and any city or county office closures as we get closer. We'll have those details for you as they're confirmed.

top.title: Bakersfield College celebrates 50th anniversary of 1976 Junior Rose Bowl title with a win
